summary: A man can make kiddushin himself or through a messenger, and so can a woman. If he gives her several dates, it matters how he says it and how much they are worth.

chunks.en: A man can make kiddushin himself or through his messenger.
chunks.st: A man can betroth a woman by himself or by means of his agent.

chunks.en: A woman can accept kiddushin herself or through her messenger.
chunks.st: Similarly, a woman can become betrothed by herself or by means of her agent.

chunks.he: הָאִישׁ מְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת בִּתּוֹ כְּשֶׁהִיא נַעֲרָה,
chunks.en: A man can marry off his daughter when she is a young girl,
chunks.explain: A na'arah is a girl just past twelve years old.
chunks.st: A man can betroth his daughter to a man when she is a young woman,

chunks.en: himself or through his messenger.
chunks.st: either by himself or by means of his agent.

chunks.en: If someone says to a woman,
chunks.st: In the case of one who says to a woman:

chunks.en: Become mekudeshes to me with this date,
chunks.explain: Mekudeshes means married to him through kiddushin.
chunks.st: Be betrothed to me with this date,

chunks.en: become mekudeshes to me with this one,
chunks.st: and adds: Be betrothed to me with that one,

chunks.he: אִם יֵשׁ בְּאַחַת מֵהֶן שָׁוֶה פְרוּטָה, מְקֻדֶּשֶׁת.
chunks.en: if one of them is worth a perutah, she is married.
chunks.st: then if one of the dates is worth one peruta she is betrothed,

chunks.en: And if not, she is not married.
chunks.st: but if not, she is not betrothed, since he mentioned betrothal in connection with each date.

chunks.en: With this one, and this one, and this one:
chunks.st: But if he said: Be betrothed to me with this one, and with this one, and with this one,

chunks.he: אִם יֵשׁ שָׁוֶה פְרוּטָה בְּכֻלָּן, מְקֻדֶּשֶׁת.
chunks.en: if all of them together are worth a perutah, she is married.
chunks.st: then even if all of them together are worth one peruta she is betrothed,

chunks.en: And if not, she is not married.
chunks.st: but if not, she is not betrothed.

chunks.en: If she was eating them one at a time,
chunks.st: If he gave her dates with the intention of betrothing her with them, and she was eating them one by one as she received them,

words.note: One by one, as she got them.

chunks.en: she is not married,
chunks.st: she is not betrothed

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בְאַחַת מֵהֶן שָׁוֶה פְרוּטָה:
chunks.en: unless one of them is worth a perutah.
chunks.st: unless one of them is worth one peruta.

summary: If a man gives kiddushin but what he gives, or what he says about himself, turns out different from what he said, she is not married. Rabbi Shimon says if it turned out better, she is married.

chunks.he: הִתְקַדְּשִׁי לִי בְכוֹס זֶה שֶׁל יַיִן,
chunks.en: Become mekudeshes to me with this cup of wine,
chunks.st: If a man said to a woman: Be betrothed to me with this cup of wine,

chunks.en: and it turned out to be honey;
chunks.st: and it was found to be a cup of honey;

chunks.en: or with this cup of honey,
chunks.st: or if he said: With this cup of honey,

chunks.en: and it turned out to be wine;
chunks.st: and it was found to be a cup of wine;

chunks.en: with this silver dinar,
chunks.st: or if he said: With this dinar made of silver,

chunks.en: and it turned out to be gold;
chunks.st: and it was found to be made of gold;

chunks.en: or a gold one,
chunks.st: or if he said: With this dinar made of gold,

chunks.en: and it turned out to be silver;
chunks.st: and it was found to be made of silver;

chunks.en: on condition that I am rich,
chunks.st: or if he said: On the condition that I am wealthy,

chunks.en: and he turned out to be poor;
chunks.st: and he was found to be poor;

chunks.en: or poor, and he turned out to be rich,
chunks.st: or if he said: On the condition that I am poor, and he was found to be wealthy,

chunks.en: she is not married.
chunks.st: she is not betrothed in any of these cases.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: if he fooled her into something better, she is married.
chunks.st: If he misled her to her advantage
chunks.stMore: by giving her something better than what he stated, or if his status was greater than he claimed, she is betrothed.

summary: If a man makes kiddushin on a condition about himself and it turns out false, she is not married, even if she says she wanted him anyway. The same is true if she fooled him.

chunks.en: On condition that I am a Kohen,
chunks.st: If one said to a woman: Be betrothed to me on the condition that I am a priest,

chunks.en: and he turned out to be a Levi;
chunks.st: and he was found to be a Levite;

chunks.en: or a Levi, and he turned out to be a Kohen;
chunks.st: or if he said: A Levite, and he was found to be a priest;

chunks.en: a nasin, and he turned out to be a mamzer;
chunks.explain: Both of these may not marry most Jews.
chunks.st: or if he said: Be betrothed to me on the condition that I am a Gibeonite, a people prohibited by rabbinic law from marrying into the congregation, i.e., from marrying a Jew of fit lineage, and he was found to be a mamzer, who is prohibited by Torah law to marry into the congregation;

words.note: From the Givonim, who were not allowed to marry most Jews.
Someone not allowed to marry most Jews.

chunks.en: or a mamzer, and he turned out to be a nasin;
chunks.st: or he said: A mamzer, and he was found to be a Gibeonite;

chunks.en: one who lives in a town,
chunks.st: or if he said: Be betrothed to me on the condition that I am a resident of a small town,

chunks.en: and he turned out to live in a big city;
chunks.st: and he was found to be a resident of a large city;

chunks.en: or in a big city,
chunks.st: or he said: A resident of a city,

chunks.en: and he turned out to live in a town;
chunks.st: and he was found to be a resident of a town;

chunks.en: on condition that my house is near the bathhouse,
chunks.st: or if he said: Be betrothed to me on the condition that my house is close to the bathhouse,

chunks.en: and it turned out to be far;
chunks.st: and it was found to be far;

chunks.en: or far, and it turned out to be near,
chunks.st: or he said: Far from the bathhouse, and it was found to be close, she is not betrothed.

chunks.en: on condition that I have
chunks.st: Or if he said that she is betrothed to him on the condition that he has

chunks.en: a grown daughter or maidservant,
chunks.st: a grown daughter or a maidservant,

chunks.en: and he does not have one;
chunks.st: and he does not have one,

chunks.en: or on condition that I do not have one,
chunks.st: or on the condition that he does not have one

chunks.en: and he has one;
chunks.st: and he has one;

chunks.en: on condition that I have no sons,
chunks.st: or on the condition that he has no sons,

chunks.en: and he has some;
chunks.st: and he has sons,

chunks.en: or on condition that I have some,
chunks.st: or on the condition that he has sons

chunks.en: and he does not have any:
chunks.st: and he does not have sons, then she is not betrothed.

chunks.en: In all of these, even if she said,
chunks.st: And in all these cases, despite the fact that she later stated:

chunks.en: In my heart I wanted to marry him anyway,
chunks.st: I intended to become betrothed to him

chunks.en: even so,
chunks.st: nevertheless, whether or not he fulfilled the condition,

chunks.en: she is not married.
chunks.st: she is not betrothed.

chunks.en: And the same if she fooled him.
chunks.st: And similarly, if it was she who misled him by making the betrothal conditional upon a statement of hers that turned out to be incorrect, the betrothal will not take effect.

summary: If a man sends a messenger to make kiddushin for him in one place and the messenger does it somewhere else, it depends on what the man meant.

chunks.en: If someone says to his messenger,
chunks.st: In the case of one who says to his agent:

chunks.en: Go and make kiddushin for me with a woman,
chunks.st: Go and betroth for me

chunks.en: so-and-so, in such a place,
chunks.st: so-and-so in such and such a place,

chunks.en: and he went and made kiddushin with her in a different place,
chunks.st: and the agent went and betrothed her in a different place,

chunks.en: she is not married.
chunks.st: she is not betrothed,
chunks.stMore: since he instructed that the betrothal take place in a particular location.

chunks.en: If he said, She is in such a place,
chunks.st: But if he said: Go and betroth the woman for me, she is in such and such a place;

chunks.en: and he made kiddushin with her in a different place,
chunks.st: and the agent betrothed her in a different place,

words.en: and he made kiddushin with her

chunks.en: she is married.
chunks.st: she is betrothed,
chunks.stMore: since he did not mean that the agent should betroth her specifically there, but was merely telling him where to find her.

summary: If a man makes kiddushin on condition that the woman has no vows or no blemishes, and she does, she is not married. If he married her without saying so, she may be sent away without her kesubah.

chunks.en: If someone makes kiddushin with a woman
chunks.st: In the case of one who betroths a woman

words.en: the one who makes kiddushin with

chunks.en: on condition that she has no vows,
chunks.explain: A vow is a promise, like not to eat a certain food.
chunks.st: on the condition that there are no vows incumbent upon her to fulfill,

chunks.en: and it turned out that she had vows,
chunks.st: and it was found that there were vows incumbent upon her to fulfill,

chunks.en: she is not married.
chunks.st: she is not betrothed,
chunks.stMore: since his condition was not fulfilled.

chunks.en: If he married her without saying anything, and she had vows,
chunks.st: If he married her without specification, and it was found that there were vows incumbent upon her to fulfill,

chunks.en: she may be sent away without her kesubah.
chunks.explain: The kesubah is the money a wife gets if the marriage ends.
chunks.st: the marriage takes effect. Nevertheless, he has the right to divorce her, and she is divorced without receiving payment of her marriage contract,
chunks.stMore: as it is assumed that he would not have married her had he known that she was limited by her vows.

chunks.en: On condition that she has no blemishes,
chunks.st: Similarly, if he betrothed her on the condition that there are no blemishes upon her,

chunks.en: and it turned out she had blemishes,
chunks.st: and she was discovered to have blemishes,

chunks.en: she is not married.
chunks.st: she is not betrothed.

chunks.en: If he married her without saying anything, and she had blemishes,
chunks.st: In a case where he married her without specification and she was discovered to have blemishes,

chunks.en: she may be sent away without her kesubah.
chunks.st: he has the right to divorce her, and she is divorced without receiving payment of her marriage contract.

chunks.en: All the blemishes that make Kohanim unfit
chunks.explain: A Kohen with certain blemishes may not serve in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: As to what is defined as a blemish, the rule is that all the blemishes that disqualify priests from performing the Temple service, as detailed in tractate Bekhorot,

chunks.en: also count for women.
chunks.st: also disqualify women from receiving their marriage contract in case of divorce.

summary: Kiddushin needs something worth a perutah for each woman. If it was less, she is not married, even if he later sent her gifts.

chunks.en: If someone makes kiddushin with two women with something worth one perutah,
chunks.st: In the case of one who betroths two women together with an item worth one peruta,
chunks.stMore: so that the value of each woman’s share was not worth one peruta,

words.en: the one who makes kiddushin with

chunks.he: אוֹ אִשָּׁה אַחַת בְּפָחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְרוּטָה,
chunks.en: or one woman with something worth less than a perutah,
chunks.st: or who betroths one woman with an item worth less than one peruta,

chunks.en: even though he later sent
chunks.st: despite the fact that he later sent

chunks.en: gifts afterwards,
chunks.explain: Sivlonos are presents a groom sends to his bride.
chunks.st: the traditional gifts [sivlonot] of a groom to the bride,

words.note: Gifts from a groom to his bride.

chunks.en: she is not married,
chunks.st: she is not betrothed,

chunks.en: because he sent them because of the first kiddushin.
chunks.st: because he sent the gifts on account of the first betrothal,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the item whose value to the woman was less than one peruta, and not to effect betrothal.

chunks.en: And the same with a boy who made kiddushin.
chunks.explain: A boy under bar mitzvah cannot make kiddushin.
chunks.st: And similarly, if there was a minor who betrothed a woman,
chunks.stMore: and he sent her gifts after he became an adult, the assumption is that he sent them on account of his betrothal when he was still a minor, and since betrothal performed by a minor is of no account, she is not betrothed.

summary: A man cannot marry a woman and her daughter, or two sisters, at the same time. A story about five women shows this.

chunks.he: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ אִשָּׁה וּבִתָּהּ אוֹ אִשָּׁה וַאֲחוֹתָהּ,
chunks.en: If someone makes kiddushin with a woman and her daughter, or a woman and her sister,
chunks.st: In the case of one who betroths a woman and her daughter or a woman and her sister

words.en: the one who makes kiddushin with

chunks.en: together, they are not married.
chunks.st: in one act of betrothal, by saying: You are both betrothed to me, neither of them is betrothed.

chunks.he: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְחָמֵשׁ נָשִׁים וּבָהֶן שְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת,
chunks.en: There was a story with five women, and two of them were sisters.
chunks.st: And an incident occurred involving five women, and among them were two sisters,

chunks.en: Someone picked a basket of figs,
chunks.st: and one person gathered a basket of figs

chunks.en: and it was theirs, and it was from Shemittah.
chunks.explain: Shemittah is the seventh year, when fields rest.
chunks.st: that were from their field, and the fruit was of the Sabbatical Year,

chunks.en: He said, You are all mekudashos to me
chunks.st: and he said: You are hereby all betrothed to me

chunks.en: with this basket,
chunks.st: with this basket,

chunks.he: וְקִבְּלָה אַחַת מֵהֶן עַל יְדֵי כֻלָּן,
chunks.en: and one of them took it for all of them.
chunks.st: and one of them accepted it on behalf of all of them.

chunks.en: And the Sages said,
chunks.st: And the Sages said:

chunks.en: the sisters are not married.
chunks.st: The sisters are not betrothed.

summary: Kiddushin with a Kohen's share of korbanos does not work. Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda argue about kiddushin with ma'aser sheni or hekdesh, depending on whether he did it on purpose or by mistake.

chunks.en: If a Kohen makes kiddushin with his share of korbanos,
chunks.st: With regard to a priest who betroths a woman with his portion of offerings,

chunks.he: בֵּין קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים בֵּין קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים,
chunks.en: whether very holy korbanos or less holy korbanos,
chunks.st: whether he did so with offerings of the most sacred order or whether he did so with offerings of lesser sanctity,

chunks.en: she is not married.
chunks.st: she is not betrothed.

chunks.en: With ma'aser sheni,
chunks.explain: Ma'aser sheni is a tenth of crops, eaten in Yerushalayim.
chunks.st: One who betroths a woman with second tithe,

chunks.en: whether by mistake or on purpose,
chunks.st: whether unwittingly or intentionally,

chunks.en: he did not make kiddushin.
chunks.st: has not betrothed her;

chunks.en: This is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: by mistake, he did not make kiddushin;
chunks.st: If he did so unwittingly he has not betrothed her,

chunks.en: on purpose, he did make kiddushin.
chunks.st: but if he did so intentionally he has betrothed her.

chunks.en: And with hekdesh: on purpose, he made kiddushin,
chunks.explain: Hekdesh is something that belongs to the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: And with regard to one who betroths a woman with consecrated property belonging to the Temple treasury, if he does so intentionally he has betrothed her,

chunks.en: and by mistake, he did not,
chunks.st: and if he does so unwittingly he has not betrothed her;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says the opposite:

chunks.en: by mistake, he made kiddushin;
chunks.st: If he does so unwittingly he has betrothed her,

chunks.en: on purpose, he did not.
chunks.st: but if he does so intentionally he has not betrothed her.

summary: Kiddushin with things we may not benefit from does not work. But if he sold them and used the money, it works.

chunks.en: If someone makes kiddushin with orlah,
chunks.st: With regard to one who betroths a woman with orla, i.e., fruit grown during a tree’s first three years,

words.note: Fruit from a tree's first three years.

chunks.en: with kilayim of the vineyard,
chunks.st: or with diverse kinds in a vineyard, i.e., grain and grapes planted together,

chunks.en: with an ox that is to be stoned,
chunks.explain: An ox that killed a person is put to death by beis din.
chunks.st: or with an ox that is sentenced to be stoned,

chunks.en: or with the eglah arufah,
chunks.explain: A calf used in a special ceremony for an unsolved death.
chunks.st: or with a heifer whose neck is broken,

chunks.en: with the birds of a metzora,
chunks.st: or with the leper’s birds which are designated for his offering,

words.note: A person with tzara'as, a skin sickness from Hashem.

chunks.en: or with a nazir's hair,
chunks.st: or with a nazirite’s hair,

words.note: Someone who promised not to drink wine or cut his hair.

chunks.en: or a firstborn donkey,
chunks.st: or with a firstborn donkey,

chunks.en: or meat cooked with milk,
chunks.st: or with meat cooked in milk,

chunks.en: or regular animals that were shechted in the Beis HaMikdash courtyard,
chunks.st: or with non-sacred animals that were slaughtered in the Temple courtyard,

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: she is not married.
chunks.st: if he betroths her with any of these items, the woman is not betrothed,
chunks.stMore: since it is prohibited to derive benefit from any of these items.

chunks.en: If he sold them and used their money for kiddushin, she is married.
chunks.st: By contrast, if one sold them and betrothed a woman with the money received from their sale, she is betrothed,
chunks.stMore: as in these cases one may derive benefit from the money he receives in exchange for the forbidden item.

summary: Kiddushin with gifts for Kohanim, or with the water and ashes of the parah adumah, does work, even by a regular Yisrael.

chunks.en: If someone makes kiddushin with terumah, ma'aser, or the Kohanim's gifts,
chunks.st: With regard to one who betroths a woman with terumot, or with tithes, or with the foreleg, cheeks, and stomach of an animal, which are given as gifts to priests,

words.note: Parts of an animal given to the Kohanim.

chunks.en: or with the special water and the parah adumah ashes,
chunks.explain: These are used to make someone tahor from tumah of the dead.
chunks.st: or with the water of purification, which is sprinkled on an impure person during the purification rite for impurity imparted by a corpse, or with the ashes of purification, which were mixed with the water sprinkled on an impure person during the purification rite for impurity imparted by a corpse, in all of these cases

chunks.en: she is married,
chunks.st: she is betrothed,

chunks.en: even if he is a Yisrael.
chunks.explain: Not a Kohen or a Levi.
chunks.st: and this is so even if the man betrothing her is an Israelite, not a priest or a Levite.
